page.title: granary: statecharts all the way down
page.description: How granary, a GitHub app, models its product, its fakes, its simulated users and its operations as statecharts, and tests all of them through their states.

hero.headline: A GitHub app that is statecharts all the way down.
hero.lede: granary listens to GitHub's issue webhooks and closes issues opened by people who are not on an allowlist. It runs in production at granary.tinyactors.dev, on @tinyactors/node. Its source and its 182 decision records are public. This page follows the statecharts through it, with a record behind each step.

section.heading: One chart per issue.
section.p: Every issue is an actor of its own, named issue/<repository>-<number>. It is spawned with what SQLite knows about the issue, asks the allowlist actor for a verdict, and either leaves the issue open or asks GitHub to close it. The chart's own comment draws it:
section.code: restore ──(phase closing)──────────────────────────────▶ closing └────(phase new | settled)──▶ idle idle ──issue.opened (phase settled)──▶ settled idle ──issue.opened──▶ checking checking ──allowlist.verdict allowed──▶ allowed checking ──allowlist.verdict not allowed──▶ closing checking ──check.timeout (10 s, send id check-timeout)──▶ failed closing (entry: <send type="github"> github.close) ──github.closed──▶ closed ──github.gave-up──▶ failed issue.opened in closing is ignored (duplicate deliveries).
section.p: Duplicate webhook deliveries, a verdict that never comes and a restart halfway through a close are states and transitions of this chart, not special cases scattered through handlers. The state is small and rebuilt from SQLite, so a crash test can kill the process and start it again.

section.heading: Tests assert on states.
section.p: granary has no unit tests. Its tests start the built application with a fake GitHub and an OpenTelemetry collector, drive it only through its webhooks and HTTP, and assert on what the actors did: which final state an issue's actor reached, and how many times.
A test that names states survives a refactor of the code behind them. It fails only when the behaviour changes.

claim.statement: The trace is the test's oracle.
claim.p: Every step of every actor is a span: the event taken, the transitions, the states entered. The harness indexes the spans and waits for a predicate such as actorFinished(address, 'closed').

section.heading: The world around it is charts too.
section.p: granary's tests run against a fake GitHub and a fake object store. Both are actor systems of their own, so their behaviour, including how they fail, is written down the same way.

item.text: One webhook delivery: sending → delivered | failed, and back to sending when it is redelivered.
One repository's issues and comments, answered in GitHub's shapes.
The faults a test injects, each with a budget: a 503 on the next close, a 403 with Retry-After, a duplicate delivery.
The fake object store's buckets, with faults of their own: latency, a dropped connection, bytes flipped at rest.

claim.p: A fault is consumed by the next matching request, so a test states how many failures the app must survive, and the relay's retries are tested against exactly that.
claim.source: ADR 0134, faults in the fake object store

section.heading: Simulated people, with a seed.
section.p: Load should look like people, not like a loop: people wait, react to what happened to their issue, escalate and give up. granary's load generator makes each simulated person an actor whose chart is its kind.

item.text: waiting → stewing → reopening → … → ragequitting → gaveUp. Its tone escalates with each closure, and it gives up after two to four.
hopeful → replying → waitingPatiently → movedOn. It replies politely once after being closed.
flooding ⇄ posting → sleeping. It opens five to fifteen issues in quick succession.
lurking ⇄ striking → retired. It injects server errors, rate limits and duplicate deliveries.
choosing ⇄ executing → cooling → exhausted. It works through edge cases: 65,536-character bodies, forged markers, malformed webhooks.

section.p: Randomness is data. Each person's seed is derived from the scenario's seed, and its generator's state lives in the chart's data, so one scenario seed reproduces every choice every person makes.

claim.statement: An oracle that does not trust the app.
claim.p: The load generator judges granary against the policy, not against granary's own records. Allowed people's issues stay open, every closed issue has exactly one comment, nothing is closed twice, and every issue that should close does, within a deadline. It would catch a granary whose bookkeeping agrees with a wrong decision.

section.heading: A watchdog that is a control loop.
section.p: granary backs itself up and exports its telemetry. Each thing it watches is a condition actor: ok → suspect → healing → ok, or attention when the remedies run out. In healing it asks a remediator for the next step on its ladder (truncating the write-ahead log, cleaning a spool, postponing a backup) and waits for the result. Each remedy is idempotent, so a crash halfway through one only means the next sample decides again.

claim.p: A condition with remedies reaches a person only after they ran out, and it returns to ok on its own when the cause clears.

section.heading: Start with one lifecycle.
section.p: Pick the lifecycle in your program that has the most flags and timers, write it as a chart, and test it on a simulated clock.
